lines: Mrs L. started out in the world's most extensive department store... they had everything.
She worked in first one department then another.
General Merchandise laid the rules for all further desk jobs within the company, so she started there.
While sitting down one day a person called her for information...
this voice belonged to a man who was extremely interesting.
Back to Mrs.L at her desk in the world's largest department store...
as she put down the phone she pulled her address book out of the drawer and went to A for Anna K....
She added it and scanned through the other people in the list. There were a total of 6584.
Her mind drifted absent mindedly and she slept....
God Bless You All!!! suddenly woke her up.... it was Princess Bride.        She asked Mrs. L
"Do you believe in heaven?"...and went on proclaiming.
Years later Mrs L was living in the UK. She was working as import agent for a company in the Ukraine
and one day found herself trying to translate the text for a new product catalogue.
This product had been imported by Mrs L in response to a valuable source of information that she had
come across while working in the world’s largest department store.
Her correspondence over this period threw some light on her choice of import business.
There has been no trace of the 'pencil' and much speculation about the darkened glasses and the comet;
was there a connection?
A large bundle of cards was found, all carefully kept and wrapped in clingfilm...
Few of the cards were signed, and many had different handwriting. They appeared
to be kept in some sort of chronological order... The images on the front of the post cards were a
fine selection: some of the usual subjects...
and at the end of the bundle they became increasingly intriguing.... for example a postcard read....
There was a whole series ostensibly about paper folding
And yet another which seemed to answer the question on a previous postcard...
One postcard had written in capital letters...
Lodged in between the postcard bundle was a piece of thin computer printout paper.
It had the following words on it...
The consequence of looking at all these cards left Mrs.L's biographer feeling as if there were
1000 people chatting in her head. This would not be the last time she felt this way...
The biographer Ms. A-Z was working for an agency called 'Find Exciting People.'
Her work was very involving. She had the ability to look into the past, present and future and
specialized in dealing with problems involving runaways and missing persons.
She also possessed the ability to contact the dearly departed.
The biographer Ms A-Z finally, began to write some notes...
"Mrs.L was born and raised in the magical city of New O; with a doctorate in meta-physics as well as
degree in Radio/TV/Film production, Mrs.L has striven to bring an understanding of the metaphysical
realms to the public through radio, television, print, and she once won $10,000 in time to avoid
serious medical problems." Mrs L had contributed the following articles to 'Myths And Facts' magazine.
The articles reveal a sincere quest into a series of interrelated subjects...
Certain quotations which touch on key thoughts are seen below, in the only remaining copies of the
magazines as cuttings made by Mrs L herself...
Ms. A-Z was an intrepid biographer wishing to see no stone unturned...
with a MINOX CAMERA she had made a photographic record of the study occupied by Mrs L over this
late period when her dealings became rather furtive or even circumspect...
On the nearest bookshelf one could just make out the following titles...
it just so happened that the biographer had a copy of this CIA book herself, she had thought it
prudent to be aware of such things... she was able to cross reference in greater detail...
the chapter headings were as follows
It went like this...
Mrs L is on the move once again...        we find her in an airport in front of a set of screens...
The business is branching out into worldwide distribution and she is researching the airline's
Cargo Destinations.
She has typed in her query and receives the following printout details
Many years later Ms. A-Z noticed on the bottom of this list of destinations in the ledger:
In this same ledger Ms. A-Z found some notes/letters believed to be from Mrs L's
little known daughter. It was on a completely different level to the rest of Mrs L's correspondence.
And a snapshot with the following in biro on the back
a card saying 'I have a bat in my chimney' had stapled to the back of it a printout with the
following instructions on it...
Ms. A-Z wrote well. She accompanied her research with detailed anecdotes...
Mrs L is enlarging her import business to worldwide distribution and it was this never
ending process that gave her a really bad headache... she tried everything to rid herself of these
wicked headaches.
She has joined a club to do with her business, there are some interesting characters in it...
she gets to know them out of curiosity, while they sit and relax in
the club room. A person called Kurt K. speaks incessantly about the New World Order
Mrs L secretly wishes to speak on subjects like Miscellaneous Miscellaneous; an obscure esoteric
class she had done at school years ago. It had inspired her with a love of things diverse
and miscellaneous
... but instead she answers him back with some tales of volcanoes and meteorite impacts...
They end up rambling on a bit... Mrs L telling him                 not long after a reply comes...
unable to take any more Mrs L departs quickly
she has a dream full of Abandoned Memories and Missing Characters...
She remembers lots of people and what they're saying clear as the light of day
When she awakes her mind goes at once to the job in hand and how it all began...
and in between typing endlessly she learned more and more about Mrs Ls very hidden talent of
predicting the future and the "King of Frightfulness" descending from the sky (presumably in France)
The significance of the events she chose was in the subjects, revisited so many times via Mrs L's
biography: travel, exploration, communications, weapons, and photography and the weather
Mrs A-Z took off her headphones and though about Mrs L going back to the root of it all,
her tenacity, her enormous archive and status as a nobody
then she started on the index.

Halloween Origami
The Models: Cats:
              Fred Rohm's Halloween Cat
                    in Best of Origami, by Samuel Randlett.
                    [Yes, this model requires cutting.]
              Toshie Takahama's Cat
                    in Classic Origami, by Paul Jackson
              Teruo Tsuji's Cat
                    in ORU #11, photo page 46, diagrams pages 128-130. [This is a two piece model and it has only one front leg.]
Bats:
              Michael LaFosse's Happy, Good Luck Bat
                    1995 OUSA Convention book (out of print :-( :-( )
                    his video Happy, Good Luck Bat & Horseshoe Crab available from Origamido
                    Origami List FTP Archive
                    Alex Barber's Website
              Tom Hull's Flapping Bat
                    On Tom Hull's Website
Witches:
              Paul Jackson's Witch on a Broomstick
                    in Festive Folding, by Paul Jackson.
                    (this model needs a bit of tweaking, but is good as is too, and pretty simple/fast to fold)
              Miyajima Noboru's Witch on a Broomstick
                    in Origami Tanteidan 4th Convention Book (pages 132-140)
                    complex and cool looking (saw one folded by a co-worker and co-folder, haven't folded it myself yet)
              David Brill's Halloween Witch
                    in Brilliant Origami, by David Brill.
                    (this model is three pieces and requires glue.)
              Kunihiko Kasahara's Witch on a Broomstick
                    in Creative Origami, by Kunihiko Kasahara
              Steve and Megumi Biddle's Flying Witch
                    in Horrorgami, by Steve and Megumi Biddle
                    (This book has been panned on the origami email list.)
              Jill Smolinski's Flying Witch
                    in Scary Origami, by Jill Smolinksi
                    (This book has also been panned on the origami email list.)
              Robert Harbin's Welch Witch
                    in The Flapping Bird, by Samuel and Jean Randlett.
              Robert Neale's Wizard and Witch
                    in Mythical Beings, by Jay Ansill
       Ghosts:
              Robert Neale's Ghost
                    in The Flapping Bird, by Samuel and Jean Randlett.
       Headless Man:
              Robert Neale's Headless Man
                    in The Flapping Bird, by Samuel and Jean Randlett.
       Pumpkins:
              Sy Chen's Pumpkin Face
                    on Sy Chen's Website.
                    Sy says that you can add lower teeth by adding an extra pleat in step 7.
              Anita F. Barbour's Pumpkin
                    on Perry Bailey's Website
       Devils/Demons:
              Jun Maekawa's Demon
                    in Viva Origami [out of print :-(].
       Skeletons:
              Marc Kirschenbaum's Skeleton
                    on the Origami List FTP Site.

1. Put a funnel type of screen on your chimney, or install a 6 inch sock
from the screen, so that bats will crawl out of the chimney thru the
funnel or sock but be unable to get back in.

2. Start a fairly small fire with the flue wide open, then add enough
green tree leaves (tree because the smoke from most tree leaves appears to
be fairly strong) to smoke them out, repeat as needed until they are all
gone, after they are gone just be sure to screen ALL of your openings down
to a size smaller than bats can navigate... as they will be looking for a
new home.

3. Another method is just to wait for cold weather, then when the bats
leave to their winter accomendations, just screen up the chimney and they
will look elsewhere to live when they return after the winter is over.
 

  In any rural area you need to be sure to close or screen any openings,
otherwise they will ALWAYS be investigated by various fauna looking for
safe havens.

"Look, there isn't any possible way to cure anyone's metaphysical dissatisfaction, because what we're dealing with here is a cosmological riddle, the likes of which no one is prepared to deal with.
Have you ever had a hair shirt woven into your skin? Yes, you have, because you and your generic code are the fabric which accumulates into self-organised garments that grasp onto the dead tree of non-being. We don't pretend to answer to the insoluble with hackney Q & A sessions which ignorantly endeavor to "get to the bottom of it".
No, the only thing that links us, you and I and everyone, is that none of us will solve the riddle of life outside of time and space by using means within time and space. So let's not bore each other with anymore desperate and ill-fated attempts at this "reality hunting", huh?
We're under oath to a tree that will someday die.
we're supposed to maintain a couple of secrets, last spoken of in the dark, damp confines of the forest. This mighty giant might at any time may fall, and with it will come the telling of many stories. The oath will be broken. Whether it is told on the forest floor or the floor boards of an A-frame house on Sturgeon Bay, or on the very paper with which you wipe your loins, the vast knowledge held now in the rings of this healthy fir will spill gloriously onto the pages  and tinto the columns and the fine print and the splendid italic font....."
